title: AF-2-part-1
description: Airframe exam covering wood structures, fabric covering, dope and finishing systems, adhesives, and related repair/inspection criteria, drawn from the AF-2 wood/fabric/finishes question/answer bank.

questions.question: What is true about regulatory minimum standards for aircraft fabric?
options: A. A performance standard does exist (it does not leave fabric unregulated)
B. No standard exists at all for aircraft fabric
C. Only foreign regulators set fabric standards
questions.explanation: Aircraft fabric is governed by performance-based minimum standards (e.g., TSO requirements), not left completely unregulated.

questions.question: What is a common factor contributing to premature glue deterioration in wood structures?
options: C. Use of stainless steel fasteners
questions.explanation: Moisture that promotes fungal growth also attacks and weakens glue joints, leading to premature deterioration.

questions.question: Saddle gussets are used to support the ends of what kind of repair?
questions.explanation: Saddle gussets reinforce and support the ends of a scarf-patch backing strip where the tapered splice meets the original structure.

questions.question: Which of the following wood defects is NOT permitted in aircraft structure?
options: A. Compression failure caused by overstress
B. Minor pin knots within allowable limits
C. Slight grain slope within allowable limits
questions.explanation: Compression failures from overstress weaken wood fibers unpredictably and are never acceptable in airworthy aircraft wood structure.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to block harmful UV rays in a finishing system?
options: C. A filler (pigmented to block UV)
questions.explanation: A pigmented filler coat helps block UV radiation from reaching and degrading the underlying fabric or wood.

questions.question: Which repair has its edges beveled at a 12:1 slope?
questions.explanation: A scarf patch uses a long, gradual 12:1 bevel so the repair piece blends structurally and aerodynamically with the surrounding skin.

questions.question: A fabric patch repair is generally used on holes not exceeding what size?
questions.explanation: Fabric patches are limited to small holes, typically up to about 1 inch in diameter, beyond which other patch types are required.

questions.question: An inherent disease occurring at the base of a tree is called what?
questions.explanation: Dote is an early stage of decay that can occur inherently near the base of a tree, distinct from mechanical defects like checks or shakes.

questions.question: What is an advantage of fabric as an aircraft covering material?
options: C. It is light in weight
questions.explanation: Fabric coverings are valued primarily for their light weight compared with metal skin, though they have durability and flammability trade-offs.

questions.question: A rupture across the wood fibers indicates what type of defect?
questions.explanation: Compression failure appears as a fiber rupture, often seen as a line running across the grain, and is an unacceptable structural defect.

questions.question: What finish is commonly used for coating and finishing in modern aviation?
questions.explanation: Polyurethane finishes are widely used in modern aviation for their durability, chemical resistance, and good appearance.

questions.question: What is used to attach fabric to the airframe structure?
questions.explanation: Fabric cement bonds the fabric envelope to the structure (ribs, formers) in fabric-covered aircraft construction.

questions.question: If the manufacturer's repair instructions are not available for a wood structure repair, what should be used instead?
options: A. Any convenient automotive repair manual
C. No repair should be attempted under any circumstances
questions.explanation: In the absence of manufacturer data, AC 43.13-1 (Acceptable Methods, Techniques, and Practices) provides generally accepted wood repair guidance.

questions.question: A spruce tree will generally not yield usable aircraft wood until it reaches at least what diameter?
questions.explanation: Spruce trees need to grow to a substantial diameter, roughly 5 feet, before the wood is suitable and usable for aircraft construction.

questions.question: Regarding wetting tests used to detect wax presence on wood, what should be avoided?
questions.explanation: Wetting tests to detect surface wax should be performed without heating the wood, since heat can alter the wax and give a false result.

questions.question: A plug patch should be used only for damage that does NOT involve what?
options: A. Supporting structure underneath the skin (such as a rib or spar)
questions.explanation: A plug patch is limited to skin-only damage; if underlying supporting structure is also damaged, a more substantial repair is required.

questions.question: Which type of patch should NOT be used to repair holes in the leading edge of the wing?
options: C. A metal skin patch designed for leading edges
questions.explanation: Fabric patches are not suitable for leading-edge repairs because of the aerodynamic and structural demands placed on that area; purpose-built repairs are required instead.

questions.question: For small finishing repair work, which application method is typically used?
options: B. Spraying with a large production gun
questions.explanation: Small touch-up or repair areas are commonly finished by brushing rather than setting up spray equipment.

questions.question: When checking a glue joint last (as a final check), what should be done?
options: A. Soak the wood in water first
B. Dry the surrounding wood (to avoid a false indication from swelling)
C. Sand the joint heavily before inspection
questions.explanation: Drying the surrounding wood before final inspection avoids misleading swelling that could mask or mimic glue joint defects.

questions.question: Which glue combines high durability with moderate-temperature curing, and offers better wet-weather and UV resistance than other adhesives, making it important in recent aircraft wood construction?
questions.explanation: Resorcinol glue cures at moderate temperatures and provides excellent durability and weather/UV resistance, making it a preferred modern aircraft wood adhesive.

questions.question: Forstner bits bore precise, flat-bottomed holes in wood regardless of their orientation to what?
questions.explanation: Forstner bits can cut clean, flat-bottomed holes at any angle to the wood grain, unlike many other bit types.

questions.question: Sitka spruce grows faster and taller in what type of climate?
options: B. A wet and moderate climate
C. A cold, dry arctic climate
questions.explanation: Sitka spruce thrives and grows most vigorously in wet, moderate (temperate coastal) climates.

questions.question: When a propeller is to be hand-carved, the blank is first marked for the leading and trailing what?
questions.explanation: Before shaping, the leading and trailing edge contour lines are marked on the propeller blank to guide the carving process.

questions.question: What is true about wash primer?
options: A. It must always be sanded before topcoating
B. It does not need sanding
C. It cannot be used on metal surfaces
questions.explanation: Wash primer is formulated to provide good adhesion without requiring sanding before subsequent coats are applied.

questions.question: What is most commonly used on rib caps after fabric covering is installed to protect and strengthen the fabric attachment area?
questions.explanation: Reinforcing tape is applied over rib caps to protect the fabric and strengthen the area where it is stitched or cemented to the ribs.

questions.question: In an I-spar repair, what is the typical slope used for the reinforcement (splice) plane?
questions.explanation: I-spar splice repairs commonly use a 5:1 taper for the reinforcement plane to gradually transfer load across the splice.

questions.question: Hard knots up to 3/8 inch in diameter are acceptable in aircraft wood if what condition is met?
options: B. They are located at the wing root only
C. They do not cause grain divergence at the edge of the flanges beyond specified limits
questions.explanation: Small hard knots are tolerated only if they don't cause excessive grain deviation around flange edges beyond the allowable limit.

questions.question: Newly developed lacquers that use a catalyst cure in what manner?
options: B. They cure only by solvent evaporation
questions.explanation: Catalyzed lacquers undergo a chemical curing reaction (cross-linking) rather than curing solely through solvent evaporation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about wood grain is true?
options: A. Any amount of grain inclination is acceptable
B. No grain inclination is ever acceptable
C. Grain inclination is acceptable up to a certain specified limit
questions.explanation: Aircraft wood specifications allow a limited degree of grain slope/inclination, beyond which the wood is rejected.

questions.question: When painting a light aircraft, where should you start?
options: A. At all corners and gaps
B. At the largest flat panel first
C. At the bottom of the fuselage only
questions.explanation: Painting typically begins at corners, edges, and gaps to ensure full coverage in hard-to-reach areas before coating the larger flat surfaces.

questions.question: Which type of patch is used to repair a hole with a diameter up to about 15 times the skin thickness?
questions.explanation: A splayed patch, with its tapered edges, is suitable for holes up to roughly 15 times the skin thickness.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about reinforcing tape?
options: A. It must always be shorter than the member it covers
B. It must be slightly longer than the member it covers
C. It is applied only to metal structure
questions.explanation: Reinforcing tape is cut slightly longer than the rib cap or member it protects, to fully cover the area including some margin.

questions.question: Which of the following is FALSE about surface tape?
options: A. That it reinforces areas subject to abrasion or stress
B. That it is applied over seams and ribs
C. That it is applied after the first wet coat of dope
questions.explanation: Surface tape is actually applied before the dope coats are built up, not after the first wet coat; it is embedded in the finishing system, not added afterward.

questions.question: Which glue type should be considered obsolete for aircraft construction?
questions.explanation: Casein glue, once common, is now considered obsolete for aircraft use due to its poor moisture and durability resistance compared with modern adhesives.

questions.question: What ensures that paint is free of dirt, water, and other contaminants before spraying?
options: C. A filter (strainer) in the paint supply line
questions.explanation: Straining/filtering paint before spraying removes contaminants like dirt and water that could cause finish defects.

questions.question: Wing spar damage can be spliced at any point EXCEPT where?
options: C. At a wing attachment fitting location
questions.explanation: Splices are not permitted through highly loaded fitting areas such as wing attachment points, where a splice could compromise the critical joint.

questions.question: The distinction between softwood and hardwood is based on what?
questions.explanation: Softwood and hardwood classifications are based on the tree's cellular/botanical structure, not on the actual hardness of the wood.

questions.question: What determines the correct weight (grade) of textile fabric to use on an aircraft?
options: A. Only the paint color desired
C. Both the maximum wing loading and the speed of the aircraft
questions.explanation: Fabric weight/grade selection depends on the aircraft's wing loading and speed, which determine the stresses the fabric must withstand.

questions.question: A radial crack that runs across the growth rings is called what?
questions.explanation: A check is a lengthwise separation of the wood that runs radially across the growth rings, typically caused by seasoning stresses.

questions.question: The period between applying adhesive and joining the assembly's parts is called what?
questions.explanation: Open assembly time is the interval after glue application during which the parts must be brought together before the glue begins to set.

questions.question: Where are aircraft registration (nationality and registration) marks typically located on a fixed-wing aircraft?
options: A. On either the vertical tail surface or the side of the fuselage
B. On the top of the wing only
C. On the landing gear doors
questions.explanation: FAR Part 45 specifies that registration marks appear on the vertical tail surface or on the sides of the fuselage (or both, depending on configuration).

questions.question: What is true about wood grain arrangement in aircraft lumber?
options: A. Some inclination of the grain is permitted within specified limits
B. Grain must run perfectly straight with zero deviation
C. Grain direction has no bearing on strength
questions.explanation: Specifications allow a limited, specified amount of grain slope because perfectly straight grain throughout is impractical, while excessive slope weakens the wood.

questions.question: What is the minimum performance standard issued by the FAA for aircraft parts used on aircraft?
questions.explanation: A TSO establishes the minimum performance standard a part (such as fabric) must meet to be approved for use on certificated aircraft.

questions.question: What is the reference wood species commonly used for aircraft construction comparisons?
questions.explanation: Sitka spruce is the benchmark (reference) species against which other acceptable substitute woods are compared for aircraft structural use.

questions.question: On a siphon-feed spray gun, where is the paint cup typically located?
options: A. On top of the gun
questions.explanation: A siphon (suction-feed) spray gun has its paint cup mounted below the gun body, with atmospheric pressure and airflow drawing paint upward.

questions.question: What is the lightest weight aircraft fabric grade recognized under the applicable FAA TSO?
questions.explanation: Among the fabric grades specified under the applicable TSO, the lightest weight classification is commonly referenced as TSO-C14b.

questions.question: Which solvent is used to slow drying and help prevent blushing of a finish?
options: B. A retarder (not quick-evaporating solvents like ethyl alcohol)
questions.explanation: A slow-evaporating retarder solvent prevents the rapid cooling that causes moisture condensation (blushing) in the finish film.

questions.question: A defect described as a compression failure running across the grain is called what?
options: A. Cross shake (or compression shake across the grain)
questions.explanation: This type of defect, running across the grain from compression failure, is categorized as a cross/compression shake and is not acceptable.

questions.question: A shake that runs longitudinally and is visible when the wood is cut tangentially through the growth rings is called what?
questions.explanation: A heart shake radiates outward from near the pith (heart) of the log and becomes visible on longitudinal/tangential cuts.

questions.question: Longitudinal cracks usually occurring between two growth rings are called what?
questions.explanation: Ring shakes are separations that occur along the boundary between two annual growth rings, running longitudinally in the wood.

questions.question: Which type of spray gun does NOT directly use compressed air to atomize the coating material?
questions.explanation: Airless spray guns atomize paint using high hydraulic fluid pressure rather than compressed air mixing with the paint stream.

questions.question: Discoloration and softening of wood are indicative of what condition?
questions.explanation: Decay caused by fungal action typically produces discoloration and a loss of wood hardness (softening).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an attribute of Sitka spruce used for aircraft construction?
questions.explanation: Sitka spruce is prized specifically because it is light in weight relative to its strength; heaviness is not one of its favorable attributes.

questions.question: Advanced decay that permits wood to be crushed into a dry powder is called what?
questions.explanation: Dry rot is an advanced stage of fungal decay that leaves the wood brittle enough to crumble into a dry powder.

questions.question: Dark discoloration or grey stains running along the grain of wood are indicative of what?
options: C. Normal aging with no concern
questions.explanation: Dark streaks or grey staining along the grain typically indicate that moisture has penetrated the wood, a precursor to decay.

questions.question: What is applied to the fabric after the fabric sealer coat has been applied?
options: C. Topcoat color only, with no filler needed
questions.explanation: After the sealer coat, a filler coat is applied to build up the finishing system and provide UV protection before color coats.

questions.question: Which adhesive is a non-gap-filling type, suitable only where surfaces can be brought into close contact (glue line no more than about 0.005 inch) under adequate pressure?
questions.explanation: Close-contact adhesives require very tight-fitting joints (glue line ≤ 0.005 in) and adequate clamping pressure, unlike gap-filling adhesives.

questions.question: What type of patch can be used to repair trimmed holes up to a 50-inch perimeter?
questions.explanation: Surface patches, cemented directly over the damaged area, are approved for larger trimmed holes up to about a 50-inch perimeter.

questions.question: What is a slow-drying solvent that can be mixed with aircraft dope to retard drying on humid days and prevent blushing?
questions.explanation: Butyl alcohol (butanol) slows the dope's drying rate, helping prevent the moisture-related blushing (clouding) effect on humid days.

questions.question: Which type of spray gun is classified as an internal-mix gun?
options: A. An HVLP (High Volume, Low Pressure) spray gun
B. A basic external-mix touch-up gun
questions.explanation: HVLP guns commonly use internal-mix nozzles, combining air and fluid inside the nozzle before atomized paint exits, improving transfer efficiency.

questions.question: A knot is described as what, structurally, within a piece of wood?
options: A. A crack caused by drying stress
B. A type of surface finish defect
C. A portion of a branch or limb embedded within the body of the tree
questions.explanation: A knot forms where a branch was once attached, becoming embedded in the trunk as the tree grew, creating a localized grain disruption.

questions.question: Aircraft decals must not be made of what material?
questions.explanation: Leather is not an approved material for aircraft decals/markings; modern decals use materials like vinyl or specially formulated films.

questions.question: What is correct about applying pressure to a joint during a glue bond?
options: A. Apply pressure only at the joint edges
B. Avoid applying any pressure to the joint
C. Apply even, uniform force/pressure across the joint
questions.explanation: Even pressure across the glued joint ensures a uniform, thin, strong glue line without starved or overly thick areas.

questions.question: When Sitka spruce is compared pound-for-pound with aluminum, what is notable?
options: A. It has about twice the tensile strength of aluminum, pound for pound
B. It is heavier than aluminum for the same strength
C. It has no measurable tensile strength
questions.explanation: On a strength-to-weight basis, Sitka spruce compares very favorably with aluminum, offering roughly twice the tensile strength per unit weight.

questions.question: What transparent protective finish is commonly used for wood?
questions.explanation: Varnish is a clear, transparent protective finish traditionally used to seal and protect wood structures while showing the grain.

questions.question: A scarf patch has its edges beveled at what slope?
questions.explanation: The long, gradual 12:1 bevel of a scarf patch provides a strong, smooth structural transition between old and new material.

questions.question: What disease develops after a tree has been felled if the timber is exposed to excessive soaking and partial drying?
questions.explanation: Post-felling decay can develop when cut timber undergoes repeated soaking and partial drying cycles, promoting fungal growth.

questions.question: In a splayed patch, the term "splayed" describes the edge slope cut at what ratio relative to skin thickness?
questions.explanation: A splayed patch's edges are cut at roughly a 5:1 taper relative to the skin thickness, less gradual than the 12:1 scarf patch slope.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct about wood used for aircraft construction regarding grain limits?
options: A. Spruce grain inclination has no specified limit
B. The limit of grain inclination for spruce is 1 inch in 15 for Grade A
C. Grade A spruce allows any slope of grain up to 1 inch in 2
questions.explanation: Grade A aircraft spruce specifications limit the slope of grain to no more than 1 inch of deviation in 15 inches of length.

questions.question: Fabric is considered airworthy until it deteriorates to what breaking strength?
options: A. Less than 70 percent of the strength required for new fabric on that aircraft
B. Less than 90 percent of new fabric strength
C. Less than 50 percent of new fabric strength
questions.explanation: Fabric is condemned once its strength falls below 70 percent of the minimum strength required when new, per standard fabric-testing criteria.

questions.question: Which type of spray gun has its paint cup mounted on top of the gun?
questions.explanation: A gravity-feed gun mounts the paint cup above the gun body so gravity helps feed paint down into the air stream.

questions.question: What provides ventilation to remove condensation at the lower ends of all fabric-covered sections?
questions.explanation: Grommeted drain holes at low points allow trapped moisture/condensation to escape from fabric-covered structure, preventing corrosion and decay.

questions.question: A fabric patch is used to repair damage up to what size?
options: A. Up to 1 inch in diameter
B. Up to 15 inches in diameter
C. Up to 50 inches in perimeter
questions.explanation: A basic fabric patch is limited to small damage, typically no more than about 1 inch in diameter.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a favorable attribute that makes Sitka spruce suitable for aircraft use?
questions.explanation: Sitka spruce is not notably flame resistant; its favorable qualities for aircraft use are strength-to-weight ratio and grain quality, not fire resistance.

questions.question: When checking a glue line for condition, what should be done regarding the surrounding wood?
options: A. Wet the surrounding wood to highlight the glue line
B. Sand away the surrounding wood entirely
C. Dry the surrounding wood to avoid a false indication caused by wood swelling
questions.explanation: Moist, swollen wood can mask or mimic glue line defects, so the surrounding wood should be dried before a reliable inspection.

questions.question: What should satisfactory glue joints in aircraft structure be able to develop?
options: A. Only partial strength under light loads
B. The full strength of the wood, under all conditions of stress
C. Strength equal to the adhesive alone, regardless of wood strength
questions.explanation: A properly made aircraft glue joint should be at least as strong as the wood itself, so the wood (not the glue line) becomes the limiting factor.

questions.question: What is used to create reinforced drain holes in aircraft fabric?
questions.explanation: Grommets reinforce the edges of drain holes cut in the fabric, preventing tearing while allowing moisture to drain.

questions.question: In general, an aircraft is certified to use a certain fabric type based on what factors?
options: B. Its wing loading and its never-exceed speed (VNE)
questions.explanation: Fabric certification/selection depends on the structural and aerodynamic loads implied by the aircraft's wing loading and VNE.

questions.question: Registration marks on a fixed-wing aircraft are NOT located on which of the following?
questions.explanation: Registration marks go on the airframe's vertical tail or fuselage sides, never on the engine itself.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of fabric covering compared with metal skin?
options: C. High cost of raw material only
questions.explanation: Fabric coverings, especially older types, are more flammable than metal skin, which is a notable disadvantage despite their light weight.

questions.question: The degree of corrosion found on screws removed from an area is indicative of what?
options: A. Water penetration into that area
B. Normal wear with no concern
questions.explanation: Corroded screws are a telltale sign that moisture has been penetrating and sitting in that area of the structure.

questions.question: Per FAR Part 45, which of the following is NOT considered an aircraft marking requirement?
options: B. Export or special marking requirements where applicable
questions.explanation: FAR Part 45 governs identification and registration marking, not weight and balance information, which is covered elsewhere (e.g., Part 23/25 and the POH).

questions.question: The ability to inspect wood structure and recognize defects cannot be learned solely by what means?
options: A. Hands-on training combined with reference material
C. Just reading a reference book
questions.explanation: Recognizing wood defects reliably requires hands-on experience and training, not just reading about defects in a book.

questions.question: When non-destructive moisture meters are used to check wood moisture content without drilling holes, what is the ideal moisture range?
questions.explanation: Aircraft wood is generally kept in the 8-12 percent moisture content range, which balances strength, stability, and resistance to decay.

questions.question: Which solvent should NOT be used as a dope thinner because its rapid evaporation cools the doped area and causes moisture to collect?
questions.explanation: Acetone evaporates very quickly, cooling the surface enough to cause condensation (blushing) in the dope film, so it is avoided as a thinner for this purpose.

questions.question: For standard certificated fixed-wing aircraft, registration marks must be at least what height?
questions.explanation: FAR Part 45 requires registration marks on most standard certificated fixed-wing aircraft to be at least 12 inches high.

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of fabric covering?
questions.explanation: Fabric coverings are generally less durable and more susceptible to damage/deterioration than metal skins over time.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a primer in a finishing system?
options: A. To provide the final color and gloss
B. To block all UV light by itself
C. To provide an anchor point for the finish coats
questions.explanation: Primer promotes adhesion, giving subsequent finish coats a solid anchor/bonding surface on the underlying material.

questions.question: What is the single most destructive element that causes polyester fabric to deteriorate?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet light breaks down the polymer structure of polyester aircraft fabric over time, making it the most destructive deterioration factor.
